<a id="ingredient-identity-and-scope"></a>
## What counts as parsley

<a id="hmi-ing-001"></a>
<a id="what-commodity-biological-species-edible-part-and-commercial-forms-does-this-page-cover"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-002"></a>
<a id="which-processing-states-and-derivatives-are-distinct-materials-rather-than-synonyms"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-003"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-can-be-transferred-between-those-materials-and-what-requires-a-separate-answer"></a>

<div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-parsley" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-parsley-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of parsley, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

dataset methods and interpretation</summary><div data-shared-evidence-content><p>Source summaries retain their original statistic, material, basis and censoring. Each source drawer identifies methods and overlapping samples. No matched reference or pooled distribution is inferred.</p></div></details><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-baseline-fallback id="hmi-reference-hmi-pooled-reference-v2:parsley-524c0876f0ac:63fe48deb3a4"><summary>HMI parsley Pb reference · Parsley, as sold</summary><div data-baseline-reference-template="hmi-pooled-reference-v2:parsley-524c0876f0ac:63fe48deb3a4"><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Reference and scope</p><p>HMI parsley Pb reference · Parsley, as sold. Parsley, as sold; As sold, as eaten or fresh weight, µg/kg; no moisture conversion. Distribution of subgroup median concentration values.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Reference (µg/kg)</th><th scope="col">Q1</th><th scope="col">Median</th><th scope="col">Q3</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Primary HMI reference</td><td>19.3–25 (bounded)</td><td>27.5–35 (bounded)</td><td>44.5–47.7 (bounded)</td></tr><tr><td>Alternative weighting</td><td>18.6–21.1 (bounded)</td><td>27–32.1 (bounded)</td><td>39.4–46 (bounded)</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p>44 reference units; 1 sampling family. Counts describe evidence units, not independent studies or certainty.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Contributing family</th><th scope="col">Reference units</th><th scope="col">Weight</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>WHO GEMS/Food</td><td>44</td><td>100%</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Methods</p><p>HMI pools subgroup medians for parsley, as sold on a as sold, as eaten or fresh weight basis: monitoring results summarized as one median per reporting region, sampling type and collection year, total diet composites and printed sample values as single observations, and printed subgroup medians from ordinary farms or markets. Each sampling family has equal total weight. Non-detects stay as zero-to-limit intervals, so quartiles carry lower and upper bounds. Means, ranges and maxima never enter as observations. Other forms, other bases, targeted sampling and results from mining, industrial, wastewater-affected, experimental, fertiliser or manufacturer settings are kept out of this reference.</p><p>Inverse weighted empirical CDF; midpoint at exact cumulative-weight boundaries. At least four reference units and a definitely positive Q1 to Q3 spread are required. This is a display eligibility rule, not statistical validation.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Limitations</p><p>WHO GEMS/Food is the only compatible sampling family for parsley, as sold on this basis in the completed parsley ledger, so this single-family reference cannot represent other markets. Reporting regions and purchase markets are not growing areas. Non-detects with differing limits widen the bounds. A position is descriptive concentration, not a safety or compliance judgment.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Admitted source families</p><ul><li><a href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants" class="internal" data-slug="sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants" data-no-cite-meta>WHO GEMS/Food</a></li></ul><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Reference version and interpretation</summary><p>Frozen evidence selection: 2026-10-22. Method: hmi-pooled-reference-v2.</p><p>hmi-pooled-reference-v2:parsley-524c0876f0ac:63fe48deb3a4</p><p>The reference is computed by HMI from admitted evidence, not copied from a study baseline. It describes the evidence currently in this scope; it is not a worldwide or current-lot benchmark. Source, year and region filters do not change it. Different HMI scopes are not one common ranking.</p></details></div></details><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-baseline-fallback id="hmi-reference-hmi-pooled-reference-v2:parsley-23f53af915de:939c2248bec5"><summary>HMI parsley Pb reference · Parsley, as sold, dry weight</summary><div data-baseline-reference-template="hmi-pooled-reference-v2:parsley-23f53af915de:939c2248bec5"><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Reference and scope</p><p>HMI parsley Pb reference · Parsley, as sold, dry weight. Parsley, as sold; Dry weight, µg/kg; no moisture conversion. Distribution of subgroup median concentration values.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Reference (µg/kg)</th><th scope="col">Q1</th><th scope="col">Median</th><th scope="col">Q3</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Primary HMI reference</td><td>280</td><td>3110</td><td>5100</td></tr><tr><td>Alternative weighting</td><td>280</td><td>3110</td><td>5100</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p>11 reference units; 3 sampling families. Counts describe evidence units, not independent studies or certainty.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Contributing family</th><th scope="col">Reference units</th><th scope="col">Weight</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>WHO GEMS/Food</td><td>9</td><td>33%</td></tr><tr><td>Altıkulaç et al. 2025</td><td>1</td><td>33%</td></tr><tr><td>Assaad et al. 2020</td><td>1</td><td>33%</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Methods</p><p>HMI pools subgroup medians for parsley, as sold on a dry weight basis: monitoring results summarized as one median per reporting region, sampling type and collection year, total diet composites and printed sample values as single observations, and printed subgroup medians from ordinary farms or markets. Each sampling family has equal total weight. Non-detects stay as zero-to-limit intervals, so quartiles carry lower and upper bounds. Means, ranges and maxima never enter as observations. Other forms, other bases, targeted sampling and results from mining, industrial, wastewater-affected, experimental, fertiliser or manufacturer settings are kept out of this reference.</p><p>Inverse weighted empirical CDF; midpoint at exact cumulative-weight boundaries. At least four reference units and a definitely positive Q1 to Q3 spread are required. <a id="sources-and-contamination-pathways"></a>
## How metals reach parsley

<a id="hmi-ing-010"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-supports-root-uptake-surface-deposition-feed-transfer-or-other-biological-pathways"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-011"></a>
<a id="what-contamination-can-arise-from-agricultural-inputs-harvesting-processing-equipment-or-packaging"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-012"></a>
<a id="which-source-attribution-claims-are-measured-modelled-inferred-or-unresolved"></a>

The evidence on how metals reach parsley comes from studies that compared exposed and ordinary settings. Parsley, as sold from Ruschita (mining area R) (mining-affected area) had lead higher at 15,800 µg/kg, against 280 µg/kg for Borlova (reference area) in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/gergen2012-banat-mining-vegetable-pca|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Iosif Gergen, Monica Harmanescu · 2012</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/gergen2012-banat-mining-vegetable-pca">Application of principal component analysis in the pollution assessment with heavy metals of vegetable food chain in the old mining areas</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Chemistry Central Journal6:156</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/gergen2012-banat-mining-vegetable-pca">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In another study, parsley, as sold from Ruschita old mining area (R) (mining-affected area) had lead higher at 15,800 µg/kg, against 280 µg/kg for Borlova reference area (Ref) in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/harmanescu2011-banat-mining-vegetables-metals|11]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Harmanescu M, Alda LM, Bordean DM, Gogoasa I, Gergen I · 2011</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/harmanescu2011-banat-mining-vegetables-metals">Heavy metals health risk assessment for population via consumption of vegetables grown in old mining area; a case study: Banat County, Romania</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Chemistry Central Journal 2011, 5:64</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/harmanescu2011-banat-mining-vegetables-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> A third study found that parsley, as sold from grown independently had total mercury higher at 7.62 µg/kg, against 6.72 µg/kg for all samples in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/fischer2022-mercury-spice-plants-poland|12]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Fischer A, Brodziak-Dopierała B · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fischer2022-mercury-spice-plants-poland">The Mercury Concentration in Spice Plants</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Processes</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fischer2022-mercury-spice-plants-poland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

These are observational comparisons from single studies; the size of the difference depends on the site, metal and distance.



<a id="ranges-by-source-region-and-variety"></a>
## Which forms and regions measured lower

<a id="hmi-ing-013"></a>
<a id="how-do-concentrations-vary-by-origin-growing-conditions-variety-and-harvest-period"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-014"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-distinguishes-within-lot-between-lot-supplier-and-production-system-variation"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-015"></a>
<a id="which-comparisons-support-a-sourcing-decision-and-where-would-geographic-or-supplier-generalization-be-unjustified"></a>

The HMI reference for lead in parsley, as sold pools 11 subgroup units from 3 sampling families, with a median of 3,110 µg/kg and a middle half spanning 280 (lower quartile) and 5,100 µg/kg (upper quartile).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source Avoiding exposed growing areas lowered the metal measured in the studies available, but no study measured the cost or supply effect of doing so.<sup class="cite">[[sources/gergen2012-banat-mining-vegetable-pca|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Iosif Gergen, Monica Harmanescu · 2012</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/gergen2012-banat-mining-vegetable-pca">Application of principal component analysis in the pollution assessment with heavy metals of vegetable food chain in the old mining areas</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Chemistry Central Journal6:156</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/gergen2012-banat-mining-vegetable-pca">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Metals do not move together, so a lot that passes a lead limit says little about cadmium, arsenic or nickel unless those are tested as well.

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-parsley" data-anchor="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-parsley" data-question="How do heavy metals get into parsley?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How do heavy metals get into parsley?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In the studies available, parsley from contaminated or exposed settings carried more metal than parsley from the same study’s control.<sup class="cite">[[sources/gergen2012-banat-mining-vegetable-pca|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Iosif Gergen, Monica Harmanescu · 2012</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/gergen2012-banat-mining-vegetable-pca">Application of principal component analysis in the pollution assessment with heavy metals of vegetable food chain in the old mining areas</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Chemistry Central Journal6:156</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/gergen2012-banat-mining-vegetable-pca">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Parsley, as sold from Borlova (reference area) (mining-affected area) had lead higher at 280 µg/kg, against 80 µg/kg for Borlova (reference area) in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/gergen2012-banat-mining-vegetable-pca|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Iosif Gergen, Monica Harmanescu · 2012</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/gergen2012-banat-mining-vegetable-pca">Application of principal component analysis in the pollution assessment with heavy metals of vegetable food chain in the old mining areas</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Chemistry Central Journal6:156</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/gergen2012-banat-mining-vegetable-pca">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-parsley" data-anchor="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-parsley" data-question="Which regions report the lowest levels in parsley?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which regions report the lowest levels in parsley?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Among GEMS/Food reporting regions, parsley, as sold had the lowest lead subgroup median in SEARO (20 µg/kg) and the highest in PAHO (370 µg/kg); reporting regions are markets, not growing areas.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> For cadmium, the lowest regional median was in EMRO (15.3 µg/kg) and the highest in EURO (190 µg/kg).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-parsley-is-inorganic" data-anchor="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-parsley-is-inorganic" data-question="How much of the arsenic in parsley is inorganic?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How much of the arsenic in parsley is inorganic?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Inorganic arsenic, the more toxic form, was measured in 2 results from 2 sources, far fewer than total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs|16]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) · 2014</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs">Dietary exposure to inorganic arsenic in the European population</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">EFSA Journal 2014;12(3):3597</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) 2014 reported inorganic arsenic at 7.9 µg/kg (mean) in parsley, as sold from European dietary-survey occurrence data.<sup class="cite">[[sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs|16]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) · 2014</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs">Dietary exposure to inorganic arsenic in the European population</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">EFSA Journal 2014;12(3):3597</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/efsa2014-dietary-exposure-iAs">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>
